subject: research/simdesign-meshmargin
professional: a senior FE stress analyst (verification-and-validation practice, NAFEMS / ASME V&V 20 style) who signs off stress-constrained bracket sizing; first checks: where and how peak stress is read (centroid vs surface/nodal), whether a mesh-convergence study supports the stated mechanism, a beam-theory hand calc of nominal stress and tip deflection, and whether the reported price changes follow from the rules or from optimiser noise

evidence.correctness: Recomputed outside the author's code (scratchpad mesh/indep.py, conv.py, vertexcheck.py, laser_b2.py; /usr/bin/python3.13, scikit-fem). (1) The README/results.txt table recomputed by my own script from experiments/results.json: all 12 rows identical (masses, prices, check ratios). (2) Mass: analytic area L*w + (H-w)*w + r^2(1-pi/4) times b times density agrees with every non-casting mass in results.json to 1.9e-7 relative. (3) Castigliano beam tip deflection (bending + Timoshenko shear + axial) vs FE check mesh: FE is 0.78-0.89 of slender-beam theory, the expected stiffening of a w x w corner block with a large fillet; nominal bending stress 6Fa/(bw^2)+F/(wb) gives Kt_eff 1.11-1.38 against the FE peak, plausible for these fillets. (4) Four experiment cells re-run with the author's task() (A CNC rules s0, B laser rules s0, B casting rules s0, A casting free s0) reproduce results.json exactly (14.086 g / 125.823 MPa etc.). (5) The README's spot check 100 -> 111 -> 121 -> 126 MPa reproduced (99.9, 110.7, 121.0, 125.8). But the quantity the conclusions rest on is biased: the peak is read at element centroids (model.py:121), which sit h/3-ish inside the surface. Reading the same P2 solution at element vertices gives 139.0, 140.3, 140.9, 141.3, 143.7 MPa for h = 2.5 ... 0.5 on that design, nearly mesh-independent, while the centroid reading climbs toward it (132.8 at h=0.5). With vertex reading at h=0.7 the B designs sit at 0.94-1.10 of the limit (README: 0.88-1.02), C at 1.14-1.20 (README: 1.06-1.11), A at 1.19-1.41. Hand calc: the A CNC rules design (w=11.61, b=3) already has nominal stress 112.9 MPa > 100 before any concentration. So the '1.3 is about right' conclusion and the overshoot figures are low by 7-15%.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: 4 tests (4 pass); experiments/run.py runs (4 cells reproduced exactly; 4249 s task time /4 cores = 17.7 min, matching 'about 20 minutes'); results.txt matches results.json; figure.py and meshmargin.svg present; homepage entry (projects.json theme simdesign) and research/README.md:541 bullet present; next steps listed. Live page https://marisstella.app/research/simdesign-meshmargin/ not reachable from this session (curl status 000 through the proxy), not counted against it. Everything it says it did, it did.
evidence.verification: `python3.13 -m pytest -q tests` (in research/simdesign-meshmargin): 4 passed in 1.8 s. The tests check the margin helper (2 tests), that centroid peak stress rises and deflection converges between h=2.5 and 1.0, and that a tighter limit makes a borderline design infeasible. Six mutants via quality_mutate.py: only with_margin '/ margin' -> '* margin' was caught; survived: the check limit taken from the margined process (run.py:41), the check solved against the margined process (run.py:39), plane-stress lambda correction removed (model.py:102, i.e. plane strain), clamp-zone exclusion removed (model.py:131), casting draft offset halved (dfm.py:71). No test pins any FE output to an analytic value or any experiment row.
evidence.craft: Read model.py, dfm.py, optimise.py, export.py, stl.py, run.py, figure.py, tests. Defects: model.py is byte-identical to simdesign-dfm's and dfm/optimise/export/stl are copied (export/stl unused here; the same engine is copied again into patchstress, gaugemesh, etc.); dead code in solve (model.py:105 'if False else None', model.py:107 unused fb); make_mesh computes the boundary-distance array only when len(grid)*len(bnd) < 4e7 and otherwise sets d = None, so h = 0.35 on a w=11.6 design crashes with TypeError (model.py:71) instead of degrading or saying so. Clean small modules otherwise, results written from code, figure parsed from results.txt.
evidence.claims: Backed by a file: every table number (results.txt), 17-35% and 1-8% mass costs (recomputed from the table: +17.2..+35.3%, +1.2..+7.9%), 'CNC and casting move at most 0.03' (0.015, 0.030), 100->126 MPa spot check, deflection <2% (test), stylised/assumed disclosure, AI-assistance note, limitations. Not backed: (a) README:44 attributes the rising peak to 'the sharp-corner stress singularities'; the peak sits on the fillet at (11.4, 19.4), no re-entrant sharp corner is in the evaluated zone, and vertex-read stress is nearly flat, so the rise is a centroid-sampling bias (this claim was later repeated as fact in research/simdesign-kirsch/README.md:38). (b) README:42 suggests the B laser price 1.220 'may partly reflect the optimiser'; it is forced by the rules: at 2 mm sheet the w/b <= 8 guard caps w at 16 mm, and w=16, b=2 carries 86.5 MPa > 76.9 MPa (B limit), so the next gauge (3 mm) is the lightest feasible stock. (c) README:43 '1.3 is about right' rests on the biased centroid reading.
evidence.fitness: A researcher building on it gets a reproducible, fast pipeline (four later simdesign-* projects did build on it). Nearest prior work, none cited: stress recovery and its superconvergent points (Zienkiewicz and Zhu, 'The superconvergent patch recovery and a posteriori error estimates', IJNME 33, 1992), grid-convergence reporting (Roache's GCI, ASME V&V 20-2009), stress-constrained sizing practice (Duysinx and Bendsoe 1998; Le et al. 2010 p-norm aggregation), Peterson's stress concentration factors (Pilkey) for fillet Kt. Against that the result is not new (a mesh knock-down on peak stress is standard practice) and its key mechanism is misdiagnosed, so a builder would inherit the wrong next step (patch averaging rather than reading surface stress). It is a one-off slug, not a step inside a PROGRAMMES.md programme, two seeds, one 2D load case, assumed rules and materials.
evidence.domain: Matches practice: P2 plane-stress elements, a check mesh finer than the search mesh, checking against the original limit, separating geometric rules from FE constraints, draft handled by analysing the narrowest section. Departs: peak von Mises read at element centroids rather than at the surface (nodal/vertex or recovered stress), which a stress analyst would flag first and which drives every overshoot number; no convergence study with Richardson extrapolation or GCI before diagnosing the mechanism; no hand-calc cross-check (the A designs fail nominal beam stress outright); polygonal 24-segment fillet; 'free' baseline only as good as two DE seeds (the A laser free 33.55 g, while the CNC-free geometry evaluated in steel is feasible at 33.05 g, price 1.070 not 1.054).

defects.what: Peak stress is read at element centroids, so every check ratio and the '1.3 is about right' conclusion carry a sampling bias: the same P2 solution read at element vertices is nearly mesh-independent (139-144 MPa vs centroid 100-133 on the spot-check design) and puts the B designs at 0.94-1.10 of the limit (README 0.88-1.02) and C at 1.14-1.20 (README 1.06-1.11); a margin of about 1.43, not 1.3, would be needed.

README attributes the rising peak to 'the sharp-corner stress singularities' (and the polygonal fillet); the peak lies on the fillet at (11.4, 19.4), no sharp re-entrant corner is in the evaluated zone, and vertex-read stress barely moves, so the stated mechanism is unsupported; simdesign-kirsch README:38 repeats it as the established mechanism.

README suggests the B laser price 1.220 'may partly reflect the optimiser' and reads it as 'not resolved at this seed count'; it is forced by the rules: at 2 mm sheet the w/b <= 8 guard caps w at 16 mm, which carries 86.5 MPa against the 76.9 MPa margined limit, so 3 mm is the lightest feasible gauge.

Four tests; five of six seeded mutants survive (check limit or process taken from the margined process, plane-strain lambda, clamp-zone exclusion removed, draft offset halved). No test pins an FE output to an analytic case or an experiment row.

No prior work on stress recovery or mesh convergence is cited or used (Zienkiewicz-Zhu SPR 1992, Roache GCI / ASME V&V 20, Peterson/Pilkey fillet Kt, stress-constrained sizing literature), no Richardson extrapolation before diagnosing the mechanism, and the project is a one-off slug rather than a step in a PROGRAMMES.md programme.

make_mesh sets the boundary-distance array to None when len(grid)*len(bnd) >= 4e7 and then compares it, so a fine mesh (h = 0.35 on a w=11.6 design) crashes with TypeError instead of working or failing with a message.
Copied engine with dead code: model.py is byte-identical to simdesign-dfm's, export.py and stl.py are copied but unused, and solve() carries 'if False else None' and an unused fb assignment.

Free baselines are only as good as two DE seeds: the A CNC-free geometry is feasible in steel at 33.05 g, lighter than the 33.55 g laser-free result, so the A laser price is 1.070 rather than 1.054; free designs for materials with the same limit could share one search.

verdict: Reproducible and honest about being stylised: my own aggregation reproduces the 12-row table from results.json, analytic masses agree to 2e-7, four re-run cells match results.json exactly, the 100 -> 126 MPa spot check reproduces, and beam theory brackets the FE tip and stress sensibly. It does not meet the bar. The study's subject is mesh dependence of peak stress, and the peak is read at element centroids: read at element vertices the same solution is nearly mesh-independent (139-144 MPa), so the reported overshoots are a sampling bias, the 'sharp-corner singularity' mechanism is unsupported, and the margined designs sit at 0.94-1.10 of the limit, not 0.88-1.02. The B laser price jump is forced by the w/b <= 8 guard at 2 mm stock, not optimiser noise. Four tests catch one of six seeded mutants, and no prior work on stress recovery or convergence is cited.
